title: Bread, wheat or cracked wheat, homemade or bakery, toasted

content.title: About
content.content: Bread made from whole wheat or cracked wheat is a whole‑grain product created from intact wheat kernels that are coarsely milled and baked into slices. It can be prepared at home or bought from a bakery and then toasted to develop a crunchy crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional method of making whole‑grain wheat bread dates back thousands of years.
Toasting intensifies aroma and creates a crisp texture that enhances flavor perception.
Cracked wheat has a lower glycemic index than white bread, making it popular in health‑focused diets.
Homemade bread allows control over salt, sugar, and additive levels.
In many cultures toasted bread is served with olive oil, garlic, or spices.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The bread delivers magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for muscle function and immune health.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Fiber and phytochemicals in whole‑grain bread may help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: A combination of protein and complex carbohydrates helps maintain fullness longer.

items.title: Wheat allergy / gluten sensitivity
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten intolerance can experience serious reactions to wheat bread.

items.title: Glycemic impact
items.content: Even whole‑grain varieties can raise blood sugar relatively quickly in some individuals.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Store‑bought bakery bread may contain higher sodium than homemade versions.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Commercial breads may include preservatives, emulsifiers, and flavor enhancers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread can be enjoyed as a snack, spread with butter, avocado, cheese, or used in sandwiches. Toasted slices pair well with soups, salads, and pâtés.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag and re‑toast directly from frozen.
